name: Silver Falls State Park
unique: Ten waterfalls on a 7.4 mile loop, and the trail walks behind four of them through basalt caverns, in a gorge cut by Silver Creek.
buzz: The Trail of Ten Falls is the hike and the behind the falls section is the reason; the winter flow is heaviest and the trail is muddy.

name: Willamette Heritage Center
unique: A woolen mill and four pioneer houses on the mill race, with working looms and the story of the Methodists who founded Salem.
buzz: The mill machinery runs on weekends and the houses are furnished; it is small and the walk along the race is pleasant.

name: Oregon State Capitol
unique: A stripped classical capitol with a gold pioneer on top and a rotunda of marble, plus a tower you can climb in summer for a view of the valley.
buzz: The tower climb and the murals in the rotunda are the two reasons to go in; it is free and the weekday sessions are open to the public.

name: Oregon Coast Aquarium
unique: A aquarium built around the Oregon coast's own habitats, with a walk through acrylic tunnel under sharks, sea otters and a seabird aviary.
buzz: The sea otters and the tunnel are the family stops; the aquarium is small enough for three hours and the pass includes the outside exhibits.

name: Newport Bayfront
unique: A working fishing bayfront where you can buy crab off the boat, watch sea lions on the docks and eat chowder in a shack over the water.
buzz: The sea lions are loud and the crab is the order; the bayfront is touristy and the working boats are still there.

name: Yaquina Head Lighthouse
unique: The tallest lighthouse on the Oregon coast, with a tidepool area below the point and a guided climb to the lens room.
buzz: The tidepools at low tide are as good as the lighthouse and the ranger tours are limited; the wind is strong and the stairs are steep.

name: Shore Acres State Park
unique: A formal garden on a sandstone bluff above a surf beach, built as the estate of a lumber baron, with a Japanese garden and a rose garden.
buzz: The garden above the surf is the photograph and the winter storm waves are the local spectacle; the garden peaks in summer.

name: Cape Arago
unique: A state park with sea lion colonies on the offshore rocks, a lighthouse and a beach, on a loop road south of Coos Bay.
buzz: The sea lions at Simpson Reef are the reason to come and the view is close; the loop road connects three state parks.

name: Samuel H. Boardman Scenic Corridor
unique: Twelve miles of the most dramatic coastline in the state, with sea stacks, a natural bridge and a trail along the cliff at every pullout.
buzz: Photographers call it the best stretch of the Oregon coast and the Natural Bridges and Secret Beach are the two stops; the trail is rough and the fog is common.

name: Gold Beach Jet Boats
unique: A jet boat up the Rogue River through rapids and canyons to a lodge lunch, with black bears, otters and eagles on the banks.
buzz: The upstream trip is the wildlife one and the fast return is the thrill; the boats are covered and the river is cold.

name: Tillamook Creamery
unique: A dairy cooperative visitor center with a viewing gallery over the cheese making floor, a scoop counter and a cafeteria of grilled cheese.
buzz: The ice cream line is the longest and worth it and the factory view is self guided; go early, the parking lot fills by noon in summer.

name: Cape Meares Lighthouse
unique: The shortest lighthouse on the coast, on a cape above sea stacks where murres and cormorants nest, with a stand of octopus tree spruce behind it.
buzz: The lighthouse and the seabird colony are the two stops and the Octopus Tree is the short walk; the parking is small and the road narrow.

name: Oregon Coast Scenic Railroad
unique: A steam train along Tillamook Bay and the coast, with open cars and a view of the water most of the way.
buzz: The open car is the seat to book and the ride is 90 minutes; the dinner train and the fall pumpkin train are the local events.

name: Wildlife Safari
unique: A drive through safari park where lions, elephants and rhinos roam in large enclosures and you stay in the car, plus a walk through village.
buzz: The drive through is the reason children love it and the animals come close to the car; the rule about keeping windows up is serious.

name: Umpqua Hot Springs
unique: A cluster of travertine pools on a cliff above the North Umpqua River, reached by a short steep trail, with a view down the gorge.
buzz: The pools are clothing optional and often busy and the trail is slick; the river below is cold and the forest is beautiful.

name: Rogue River Jet Boats
unique: A jet boat through the Hellgate canyon and rapids south of Grants Pass, with stops at a lodge and wildlife on the banks.
buzz: The Hellgate trip is the half day standard and the fast spins are the fun; bring a jacket, the river spray is cold.

name: Oregon Caves
unique: A marble cave system with a tour through passages and a 1930s lodge at the entrance, reached by a winding road through the Siskiyous.
buzz: The cave tour is ranger led and needs a ticket and the marble formations are the highlight; the road is narrow and the cave is 42 degrees.

name: Wallowa Lake Tramway
unique: The steepest four passenger gondola in North America, climbing 3,700 feet to the top of Mount Howard for a view of the Wallowa Mountains and Hells Canyon.
buzz: The view from the top is the reason to ride and the trail along the summit is easy; the tram is weather dependent and the tickets are not cheap.

name: Joseph Bronze Foundries
unique: A town of bronze foundries where you can watch a sculpture being cast and see finished pieces on the main street, in a valley below the Wallowas.
buzz: The foundry tours are the reason art people stop and the main street galleries are free; check hours, the foundries run on production schedules.

name: Zumwalt Prairie
unique: The largest remaining bunchgrass prairie in North America, where hawks and eagles nest in the canyon rims and the grassland runs to the horizon.
buzz: The raptors in spring are the reason to come and the preserve is quiet; the roads are gravel and the weather changes fast.

name: Oregon Trail Interpretive Center
customer: History families, school groups, road trippers
unique: A center on the last mountain crossing of the Oregon Trail, with life size wagon displays, a trail you can walk and the ruts still cut into the sagebrush.
buzz: The wagon and the ruts are the reasons to stop and the ranger talks are good; it is a couple of miles off the interstate and worth the detour.

name: Sumpter Valley Railroad
unique: A restored narrow gauge logging railroad with a steam Heisler locomotive, running through the gold dredge country of the Blue Mountains.
buzz: The steam engine and the open cars are the fun and the dredge is a short drive away; the ride is short and the volunteers run it.

name: Malheur National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A 187,000 acre wetland in the high desert where 320 bird species have been recorded and sandhill cranes stage by the thousands in spring.
buzz: The spring crane migration is the event and the auto tour route is the way to see it; the refuge is remote and the nearest town is 30 miles.

name: Steens Mountain
unique: A 30 mile fault block mountain rising a mile above the Alvord Desert, with a road to a 9,700 foot overlook of the gorge and the playa below.
buzz: The drive to the top and the Kiger Gorge overlook are the experience; the road is rough and the mountain is snowed in most of the year.

name: Columbia Gorge Discovery Center
unique: A museum on the gorge's geology, ice age floods and the Lewis and Clark route, with live raptors and a trail into the oak woods.
buzz: The raptor center and the flood geology are the reasons to stop; it is a good rainy day alternative to the waterfalls.

name: Rowena Crest
unique: A viewpoint on the old Columbia River Highway where the road loops over a bluff above the gorge, with wildflowers in spring and a trail along the rim.
buzz: The loop road is the photograph and the balsamroot in April is the season; the wind is strong and the pullout is small.

name: Fort Clatsop
unique: A replica of the winter fort where Lewis and Clark's expedition stayed in 1805, with ranger demonstrations, a canoe and trails through spruce forest.
buzz: The ranger talks and the flintlock demonstrations are the family draw; the fort is a reconstruction and the site is quiet in winter.

name: Astoria Column
unique: A 125 foot column painted with a spiral history of the west, on a hill above the Columbia mouth, with a viewing deck and balsa planes to throw.
buzz: The climb is 164 steps and the view of the river meeting the Pacific is the reason; the tradition of launching wooden planes from the top is real.
